chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When a man divorces his wife by Khul'a, it is one irrevocable divorce, and he is a suitor among the suitors. It is not permissible for him to divorce her by Khul'a until she is the one who seeks that from him, without him having beaten her, and until she says: 'I shall not fulfill a vow for you, nor wash for you from major impurity, and I will bring into your house the one you dislike, and I will settle in your bed, and I will not establish the limits of Allah.' So when this is from her, then what he takes from her is suitable/permissible.

key_terms.خَلَعَ: Khul'a (compensatory divorce initiated by the wife)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific conditions required for a Khul'a divorce to be valid according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes that Khul'a is fundamentally a wife-initiated procedure, requiring the husband to have not inflicted harm (darar) to justify the compensation. It specifies that the wife must declare her intent to cease fulfilling core marital duties—such as sexual intimacy and obedience—to validate the husband's acceptance of the price, reflecting the Shia juristic view of Khul'a as a mutual dissolution rather than a unilateral revocation.
